news.headline: Gharibwal Cement halts clinker production after kiln fan damage
news.summary: Gharibwal Cement Limited (PSX: GWLC) temporarily stopped clinker production after its kiln ID fan was damaged during operation, per Mettis Global. Replacement ID fan and parts already procured from the manufacturer, with shipment expected next month; a Letter of Credit has been opened. No production-loss figure or resumption date disclosed. Logged as impact 2 (minor company operational item - temporary, remediation already underway).

news.headline: Federal Constitutional Court allows tax credit adjustment against super tax
news.summary: Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court ruled that tax credits granted under Section 168 of the Income Tax Ordinance can be legally adjusted against super tax liability, setting aside a prior Islamabad High Court decision that had denied this to private mobile operator Zong (not a PSX-listed universe ticker) in its dispute with the FBR. Six-page judgment authored by Justice Aamer Farooq holds the tax credit is a 'separate and established legal right' and that fiscal law should be interpreted to facilitate taxpayers. Ruling sets a precedent applicable to corporate taxpayers broadly (banks and other large corporates subject to super tax), potentially reducing effective super-tax cash outflow for eligible taxpayers with unadjusted tax credits. Logged as impact 4 (material regulatory/judicial action with broad corporate-tax implications) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10); escalation flagged.

news.headline: PSX confirmed close: KSE-100 settles at 177,955.51, down 2,546.94 points (-1.41%)
news.summary: Confirms/supersedes the earlier same-day unconfirmed checkpoint (DPS 178,211.92/-2,290.52 vs Mettis 177,955.51/-2,546.94, both captured ~3:30-3:38pm PKT and already logged). Per The Express Tribune ('PSX tumbles 1,806 points amid geopolitical tensions'), the confirmed close matches the Mettis figure: KSE-100 plunged 2,546.94 points (-1.41%) to settle at 177,955.51, from Monday Aug 17's confirmed close of 180,502.45; intraday high 180,602.44, low 177,866.04. Drivers cited: fading prospects for a US-Iran peace deal, oil prices near three-week highs on supply-risk concerns, and domestic unease after the Supreme Court ordered former PM Imran Khan's transfer from jail to hospital for medical treatment. Selling was broad-based across commercial banks, oil & gas exploration, oil marketing companies, cement, automobile assemblers, and power generation; the article names United Bank (UBL), Fauji Fertiliser (FFC), Meezan Bank (MEBL), Engro Holdings (ENGROH), OGDC, PPL, Hub Power (HUBC) and Mari Energies (MARI) as heavyweights under pressure, and Cnergyico PK (CNERGY) as volume leader (231.5m shares, -Rs0.22 to Rs14.79). Volume 1.03bn shares, value Rs50.7bn; of 494 companies traded, 104 advanced/368 declined/22 unchanged. Tagged to the union of the superseded item's tickers (MACRO) plus all tickers newly named in this source, per the confirmed-close supersession rule. Impact 4 (material market-wide move, >1% single-session decline with named heavyweight movers).
